chunks: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel except what Israel (Jacob) forbade upon himself before the Torah was revealed.
Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."

key_terms.إِسْرَائِيلُ: Jacob (peace be upon him), also known as Israel

ai.seo_question: What dietary restriction did Jacob impose on himself before the Torah was revealed?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between *haram* (divine prohibition) and *haram ala nafsihi* (self-imposed prohibition), illustrating how Jacob’s voluntary asceticism due to illness was later codified as a general dietary law in the Torah. The Quranic challenge to the Jews to produce the Torah and recite it serves as a rhetorical proof of their claim, while also affirming the general permissibility of food prior to specific divine legislation.

en.ahmedali: To the children of Israel was lawful all food except what Israel forbade himself before the Torah was revealed.
Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if what you say is true."
en.ahmedraza: All food was lawful for the Descendants of Israel (Jacob), except what Israel forbade for himself, before the Taurat (Torah) was sent down;
say, “Bring the Taurat and read it, if you are truthful.”
en.arberry: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel save what Israel forbade for himself before the Torah was sent down.
Say: 'Bring you the Torah now, and recite it, if you are truthful.'
en.daryabadi: Every foods was allowable unto the Children of Isra'il, save that which Isra'il had forbidden unto himself, ere the Taurat was revealed.
Say thou: bring ye then the Taurat and recite it, if ye say sooth.
en.hilali: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Taurat (Torah) was revealed.
Say (O Muhammad SAW): "Bring here the Taurat (Torah) and recite it, if you are truthful."
en.itani: All food was permissible to the Children of Israel, except what Israel forbade for itself before the Torah was revealed.
Say, “Bring the Torah, and read it, if you are truthful.”
en.maududi: All food (that is lawful in the Law revealed to Muhammad) was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful to themselves before the revelation of the Torah.
Tell them: 'Bring the Torah and recite any passage of it if you are truthful.'
en.mubarakpuri: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Isra'il made unlawful for himself before the Tawrah was revealed.
Say: "Bring here the Tawrah and recite it, if you are truthful. "
en.pickthall: All food was lawful unto the Children of Israel, save that which Israel forbade himself, (in days) before the Torah was revealed.

en.qarai: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden himself before the Torah was sent down.

en.sahih: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed.

en.sarwar: All food was lawful for the children of Israel except for what Israel had deemed unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed.
